page: Microsoft Azure E112ibs_v5 is an isolated, block-storage-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine features 112 dedicated vCPUs derived from 56 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It operates at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz and includes 48 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 6.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external premium block storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The E112ibs_v5 achieves strong results in multi-core stress-ng testing and Passmark CPU evaluations, particularly in the encryption test where it ranks in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is also a key strength, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 5839.55 GB/sec and large block uncached read speeds at 335.8 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations also show strong performance. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E112ibs_v5 offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads that require dedicated compute resources without the overhead of local physical disks. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a specialized choice for workloads dependent on network-attached block storage. This server is highly suited for large-scale database operations, memory-cached applications, enterprise-grade web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
